dishes.name: Tielle sétoise
dishes.desc: A slightly brioche-like pie filled with octopus, tomato, onion, chilli and white wine, a recipe brought by fishermen from Gaeta. A Sète speciality that Montpellier has adopted.

dishes.name: Petits pâtés de Pézenas
dishes.desc: Spool-shaped pastries mixing lamb with lemon and brown sugar, sweet and savoury at once. Pézenas has made them since the 18th century and eaten slightly warmed as a starter.

dishes.name: Macaronade sétoise
dishes.desc: A Sète dish of macaroni with slow-cooked beef brageoles, pork and tomato sauce, hearty and traditional on the Hérault coast.

dishes.name: Brasucade de moules
dishes.desc: Mussels from the Thau lagoon cooked in a big pan over a vine-cutting fire, doused with scented olive oil and eaten with the fingers.

dishes.name: Oreillettes
dishes.desc: Thin, crisp fritters made from a doughnut-type dough and dusted with sugar, served at traditional festivals and sold at Montpellier bakeries.
